record.original_question: Understand how virtual-knot polynomials relate to Vassiliev invariants for virtual knots, and determine whether every finite-type Vassiliev invariant of classical knots extends to a finite-type invariant of long virtual knots in the sense described by the paper, while also clarifying the alternate finite-type notion for virtual knots mentioned there.

evidence.quote: Understand the connection between virtual knot polynomials and the Vassiliev knot invariants of virtual knots (in Kauffman's sense).
Does every Vassiliev invariant of finite type, for classical knots extend to an invariant of finite type for long virtual knots?
This alternate formulation needs further investigation.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions.

(a) A virtual knot diagram is a 4-valent planar graph whose vertices are decorated as either classical crossings (with over/under information) or virtual crossings (drawn as a small circle). Virtual knots are equivalence classes of virtual knot diagrams modulo the generalized Reidemeister moves: the three classical Reidemeister moves R1, R2, R3, the three purely virtual moves V1, V2, V3, and the mixed move M (a classical strand passing across a virtual crossing). A long virtual knot is the analogous equivalence class of virtual diagrams of a 1–1 tangle (with two fixed endpoints at infinity).

(b) Following Kauffman, a singular virtual knot is a virtual diagram that, in addition to classical and virtual crossings, has finitely many rigid 4-valent transverse double points ("singular crossings"). Any invariant v of virtual knots taking values in an abelian group is extended to singular virtual knots by the Vassiliev skein relation
   v(D_×) = v(D_+) − v(D_−),
where D_+, D_− are the two classical resolutions of a singular crossing. The invariant v is called a Vassiliev (finite-type) invariant of degree ≤ n (in Kauffman's sense) if its extension vanishes on every singular virtual knot with more than n singular crossings. The same definition is made for long virtual knots.

(c) There is also an alternate finite-type notion for virtual knots in which the role of singular crossings is played by an additional "semi-virtual" resolution, defined by the relation
   v(D_×) = v(D_+) − v(D_v),
where D_v denotes the diagram obtained by replacing the classical crossing by a virtual crossing.

Problems.

1. Establish the precise relationship between the standard polynomial invariants of virtual knots (such as the Jones polynomial, the bracket polynomial, and their virtual generalizations) and the Vassiliev finite-type invariants of virtual knots in Kauffman's sense (b): determine, for each such polynomial, the filtration by finite-type degree of its coefficients (after a suitable substitution like x = e^h).

2. Decide whether every finite-type Vassiliev invariant of classical knots (of degree ≤ n) extends to a finite-type invariant of long virtual knots of the same degree, in Kauffman's sense.

3. Compare the Kauffman finite-type theory (b) with the alternate finite-type theory (c) for virtual knots, and determine the precise relationship between the resulting filtered algebras of invariants.
artifact.status_search_result: There has been substantial progress on connections between virtual knot polynomials and Vassiliev-type invariants in Kauffman's sense, and on the alternate "GPV" finite-type theory due to Goussarov–Polyak–Viro, including weight-system results from the Jones polynomial. However, the literature continues to treat the full classification problem and the question of whether every classical finite-type invariant extends to a long virtual finite-type invariant of the same degree as not fully resolved, and recent work (e.g., on V₁/V₂ polynomials of long virtual knots and on knotoid finite-type invariants from 2020–2025) builds on rather than closes these questions. The status is therefore best described as partially solved / still under active investigation.

status_evidence.title: Finite Type Invariants of Classical and Virtual Knots (Goussarov–Polyak–Viro)
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces an alternate finite-type theory for virtual knots and long virtual knots based on virtualization, distinct from Kauffman's singular-crossing definition.
status_evidence.claim: An alternate finite-type theory for (long) virtual knots exists and is studied alongside Kauffman's; the comparison continues to be investigated.

status_evidence.title: The V₁- and V₂-polynomials of a long virtual knot
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work analyzing polynomial invariants of long virtual knots and their finite-type behavior.
status_evidence.claim: Active recent research on polynomial invariants of long virtual knots and their relation to finite-type invariants.

status_evidence.title: Finite type invariants for knotoids
status_evidence.snippet: Develops finite-type invariants in a related (knotoid) setting, indicating that extension/comparison questions remain a current topic.
status_evidence.claim: Finite-type extension and comparison questions in virtual/long settings remain an ongoing research area.

status_evidence.title: Virtual Knot Theory (Kauffman)
status_evidence.snippet: Defines Vassiliev invariants for virtual knots via singular crossings and discusses graphical finite type from the Jones polynomial.
status_evidence.claim: Kauffman's definition and partial polynomial-to-finite-type results are established.
